source.title: Convergence Rates for Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability in Overparametrised Least Squares
source.authors: L. MacDonald; Han-Cheng Min; Leandro Palma; Salma Tarmoun; Zi-Qing Xu; René Vidal

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes gradient descent above and around the stability threshold and reports convergence behavior, using a depth-5 width-1 scalar-factorization least-squares problem rather than the wide networks in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence results and numerical demonstrations for three learning-rate regimes. The experiments use five initializations, shown together in figures. Other cited studies' results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study proves recovery from initial instability and convergence under full-batch GD above an initial local stability threshold, bearing on V5 through a codimension-one least-squares model. Its numerical example is a width-one linear network, so it does not establish the wide-network claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate under the stated local regularity, invariance, genericity and sharpness-convexity assumptions. Subcritical GD converges linearly to a minimum with suboptimal sharpness; critical GD converges by a power law to the sharpness-minimizing solution; slightly supercritical GD converges linearly to a period-two orbit around that solution. Extension from standard initialization remains conjectural.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient descent on squared loss and studies learning rates around or above the stability threshold, but analyzes a depth-5 width-1 scalar-factorization toy problem rather than wide networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes across subcritical, critical, and supercritical learning-rate regimes.
record.problems: The numerical demonstrations concern a single depth-5, width-1 scalar-factorization problem with target y = 1 and five initializations. The theory assumes initialization sufficiently near the solution manifold; the paper says standard initialization may not satisfy this and leaves that question for future work. No training-loss values are reported for the supercritical orbit.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network classification error on CIFAR, corrupted labels, model size, regularization and optimizer comparisons.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, training speed and trainable depth.

Wide networks; the initial linearized-model threshold specifically; a measured initial loss spike; progressive sharpening toward the threshold from standard initialization; divergence at substantially larger rates; divergence from initially stable runs; and the training-loss magnitude on the supercritical orbit.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup's training speed, stability and learning-rate tolerance.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. R3 warrants no verdict that low-loss recovery fails: nonzero limiting loss need not be large loss. Likewise, the untested wide-network setting and standard initialization are untested scope, not adverse results.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer comparisons, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and training error as depth changes.

Wide networks, linearized-model stability limits, sharpness hovering in full-batch training, and runs diverging from below the threshold are not tested. The study analyzes a depth-5 width-1 scalar-factorization least-squares problem.
Batch normalization comparisons, accuracy speed, and learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: depth 5, width 1 scalar factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on least-squares loss in the subcritical regime, with five initializations shown.
rows.measure: Convergence to a global minimum after transient instability; convergence rate O(β^t), with suboptimal sharpness.
rows.value: The iterates converge to a global minimum in M at rate O(β^t); initial instability is overcome in finite time.
rows.note: The theorem states convergence under its assumptions; Figure 2 shows trajectories from five initializations. The model is a scalar-factorization toy problem, not a wide network.
rows.check: Specify 2/λ(θ0∥) < η < 2/λ(θ*∥), with a sufficiently small excess above the initial threshold and initialization sufficiently near the solution manifold. Sharpness decreases below 2/η in finite time, followed by convergence to zero loss. The theorem covers qualifying codimension-one problems; depth five and width one describe the numerical demonstration.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Theorem 5.1 and Figure 2; Appendix F confirms depth 5, width 1 and target y = 1.

rows.subject: depth 5, width 1 scalar factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on least-squares loss at the critical learning rate, with five initializations shown.
rows.measure: Distance to the sharpness-minimizing global minimum and magnitude of the orthogonal coordinate; both stated as Θ(t−1/2).
rows.value: The iterates converge to the optimally flat global minimum with power-law rate; dM(θt∥, θ∗∥) = Θ(t−1/2) and |θt⊥| = Θ(t−1/2).
rows.note: The theorem applies to sufficiently close initial conditions under its additional hypothesis. The figure shows trajectories from five initializations.
rows.check: Critical means η = 2/λ(θ*∥), the threshold at the sharpness-minimizing solution, rather than the initial stability threshold. Under the local assumptions, convergence to a global minimum establishes zero limiting loss despite persistent oscillatory dynamics. Distinguish the general theorem from the depth-five numerical example.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Theorem 5.2 and Figure 3; Appendix F confirms depth 5, width 1 and target y = 1.

rows.subject: depth 5, width 1 scalar factorisation problem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on least-squares loss in the supercritical regime, with five initializations shown.
rows.measure: Asymptotic behavior of the iterates and convergence of the tangent coordinate toward the sharpness-minimizing point.
rows.value: The iterates converge to a stable period-two orbit orthogonal to M; the tangent coordinate converges linearly to the sharpness-minimizing global minimum.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says the complete iterates do not converge to a global minimum in this regime. It does not state a training-loss value for the orbit.
rows.check: The stable period-two orbit and linear convergence toward it are established for η slightly above 2/λ(θ*∥) and restricted nearby initializations. However, failure to converge to an exact global minimum does not establish failure to reach low training loss. No orbit-loss value or comparison establishes V5's low-loss outcome; the extracted partial state overinterprets parameter nonconvergence.
